verified_by: 3-state differential over the project's OWN adaptation method, ZmsSyncer.setupJsonParserLimits(), built from their real Maven reactor (mvn -pl syncers/zms_aws_domain_syncer -am, JDK 21) and run on JDK 21.
note: THE STRONGEST CASE IN THIS SET, and the first found by deliberately routing around a bias in the discovery method rather than in spite of it. Six days from bump to fix, a direct version declaration in the root pom, a 997-star upstream project, and state 3 executes the client's own method rather than a reconstruction of it.
discovery_method: CODE SEARCH plus file-history walking. Commit search never returned AthenZ -- it was not among the 82 repos that search found, and a repo-scoped commit search for the identifier returns zero, because GitHub's commit index does not cover this repository's history. Code search for '"setStreamReadConstraints" language:java' returned 241 repos, 238 of them unseen by commit search; walking the introducing commit of each candidate file then dated AthenZ's adaptation to 2023-06-08, inside the crossing window.
why_the_discovery_method_matters: Commit search is biased toward recent commits. Across this break its results were 2021:1, 2023:2, 2025:13, 2026:83 -- 83 of 99 from the current year, three years after the boundary. That is not how adaptation behaves; it is an index artefact. Since cases cluster NEAR the boundary by definition, commit search systematically under-samples exactly where they are. File history via the commits API is complete per path and has no such bias, which is why it found this case immediately.

library._baseline_note: Their ACTUAL previous version, taken from the same pom property they bumped -- not a stand-in.
library.dependency_scope: compile, declared directly as <jackson-core.version> in the root pom.xml

in_repo_version_transition.mechanism: direct bump of the <jackson-core.version> property in the root pom.xml
in_repo_version_transition.bump_commit_message: update java and go dependencies to their latest releases
in_repo_version_transition.elapsed: 6 days from crossing to fix -- the tightest of any case with a traced crossing
in_repo_version_transition.why_the_pipeline_did_not_find_it: The break was never mined. Only 7 rows were ever classified for this catalog entry. Separately, commit search cannot index this repository's history, so the adaptation-axis search could not have surfaced it either.

bump_source: jackson-core 2.15.0 release notes; StreamReadConstraints. The library itself raised maxStringLength from 5M to 20M in 2.15.1 after user reports, which is independent evidence the default bit people.

behavioral_break.mechanism: jackson-core 2.15.0 introduced StreamReadConstraints with parser limits applied BY DEFAULT: maxStringLength (5M in 2.15.0, 20M from 2.15.1), maxNestingDepth 1000, maxNumberLength 1000. JSON that 2.14 parsed fine now throws com.fasterxml.jackson.core.exc.StreamConstraintsException at parse time. Nothing on the client's path changes signature, so the client compiles unchanged and fails at run time.
behavioral_break.why_it_breaks: Same as `mechanism`; recorded under both names because older cases in this directory use `why_it_breaks` and newer ones use `mechanism`.
behavioral_break.affected_class: com.yahoo.athenz.zms.ZMSImpl and com.yahoo.athenz.zts.ZTSImpl (their JSON mappers), plus the syncer's ZmsSyncer
behavioral_break.observed_exception: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.exc.StreamConstraintsException: String length (20051429) exceeds the maximum length (20000000)
behavioral_break.blast_radius: Clients parsing JSON with a string field above the default. For AthenZ that is routine -- their own config comment says the raise exists 'to support large domains that may exist in Athenz'.

adaptation.repo_note: Yahoo/Verizon Media's authorization service (ZMS/ZTS). 997 stars, upstream, not a fork. Multi-module Maven.
adaptation.commit_message: increased/configure json string limit for jackson (#2203)
adaptation.why_that_matters: Their default for maxStringLength is 200000000 -- ten times the library's 20M -- so the limit is genuinely lifted rather than exposed as a knob at the library value. Their own config comment states the reason: 'we increase this value to 200GB to support large domains that may exist in Athenz'.
adaptation.evidence_of_diagnosis: They left maxNestingDepth and maxNumberLength at the library's own defaults (1000/1000) and raised ONLY maxStringLength. A blanket hardening or a careless copy would have moved all three; raising exactly the one that broke them indicates the failure was diagnosed.
adaptation.scope: 8 files across three services -- a coordinated response, not an incidental edit inside a larger change.

verification.method: Built the syncer module and its reactor dependencies with their own Maven build at both commits (mvn -B -pl syncers/zms_aws_domain_syncer -am -DskipTests test-compile). A driver in their package calls ZmsSyncer.setupJsonParserLimits() directly -- the method is package-private and uses no instance state, and their three-arg constructor skips the AWS setup the no-arg one performs -- then parses JSON with a 25 MB string field through a plain ObjectMapper. The override is JVM-global, which is exactly how their servers rely on it.
verification.test: AthenzBbcDriver.java (authored trigger, THEIR adaptation). Nothing of ours is substituted for their logic: the 200000000 value comes from their own Config.DEFAULT_JSON_MAX_STRING_LENGTH via putIfAbsent. We supplied only their expected deployment layout -- an empty ${root}/zms_syncer/conf/zms_syncer.conf -- so that their own defaults load.

states.name: 2_broken
states.result: THREW StreamConstraintsException: String length (20051429) exceeds the maximum length (20000000)

states.name: 3_adapted
states.config: adapted code + jackson-core 2.15.2, their setupJsonParserLimits() applied

verification.isolation: States 2 and 3 share the jackson-core 2.15.2 jar, so the only variable is their own commit. States 1 and 2 share their code, so the only variable is the library version -- and both versions are theirs, from the pom property they bumped.
threats_to_validity: THE TRIGGER IS AUTHORED, not their test. The adaptation under test is entirely AthenZ's; only the oversized JSON document and the main() that invokes their method are ours. Their suite has no 25 MB fixture, for the same reason no project does.

STATE 3 DRIVES THE SYNCER'S COPY of the adaptation, not ZMSImpl's or ZTSImpl's. All three call the same StreamReadConstraints.overrideDefaultStreamReadConstraints with the same 200000000 default; the syncer was chosen because ZMSImpl and ZTSImpl require full server construction. The mechanism verified is identical.

JACKSON-DATABIND AND -ANNOTATIONS were matched to the core version in each state (2.14.2 with 2.14.2, 2.15.2 with 2.15.2). Mixing them produced a ClassNotFoundException for StreamConstraintsException, which is a version-skew artefact and not the break; the matched pairing is what their pom resolves.
